text.en: On a long trip you do not always need the exact number. You often need a good guess quickly.

An estimate is a number close to the exact answer. We find it by rounding the numbers to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand.
To round to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit. If it is 5 or more, go up; if less than 5, stay. So 2,346 rounds to 2,300.
To round to the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit. 2,346 rounds to 2,000, and 2,500 rounds to 3,000.
To estimate a sum, round both numbers first. 4,860 + 3,150 is about 5,000 + 3,000 = 8,000.
In the book we also choose two numbers whose sum is closest to a target such as 10,000, by rounding and checking.
An estimate helps us check if the exact answer is reasonable. If 5,205 + 6,220 came out as 1,142, the estimate 5,000 + 6,000 = 11,000 would warn us.
